mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -65.4% over the last week after declining from -71.4% three weeks ago. This plateau signals exhaustion of downward momentum. Absent further shocks, mean-reversion toward baseline will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility at -60.6% (up 3.3 points from t-1w) signals growing commuter confidence. Rising transit use over the next two weeks will trigger increased retail foot traffic as workers resume shopping during commute windows, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -62.7% to -60.6% in one week
failure_condition: TRANSIT fails to improve by more than 2 percentage points in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to baseline despite TRANSIT improvement.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility at -29.3% is substantially less suppressed than RETAIL_REC at -65.4%, indicating outdoor recreation is already recovering. This behavioral shift toward outdoor activities will compete with indoor retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS suppression is 36 percentage points less severe than RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days while PARKS remains stable or declines.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES at -53.0% shows persistent suppression with minimal week-on-week improvement (only 2.6 points from t-1w). Continued workplace restrictions signal ongoing policy constraints that will prevent retail recovery, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -50% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has not improved more than 3 percentage points in any single week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises more than 10 percentage points in a single week, or RETAIL_REC rises more than 8 percentage points over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM at -28.4% shows essential-goods mobility is nearly normalized. When essential shopping stabilizes, consumers redirect discretionary spending to retail-and-recreation. This substitution effect will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next week as pent-up demand releases.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -28.4% is closest to baseline of all categories
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below -30% in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL at 16.7% remains elevated, indicating people still spend excess time at home. High residential occupancy suppresses retail mobility. Only when RESIDENTIAL falls below 10% will retail recovery accelerate. Over the next four weeks, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has declined only 0.3 percentage points over three weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises more than 10 percentage points over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT (-60.6%, up 3.3 points) and WORKPLACES (-53.0%, up 2.6 points) signals coordinated return to commuting. This dual recovery will compound retail foot traffic: commuters shopping en route to work plus increased weekday retail hours. RETAIL_REC will rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by more than 2 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES declines in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not rise by at least 3 percentage points over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July in Lombardy marks peak summer holiday season. RETAIL_REC suppression at -65.4% reflects vacation departures and reduced urban retail demand. Over the next four weeks (late July through mid-August), holiday exodus will intensify, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed despite any policy reopening.
evidence_refs: fact:decision point is 2020-07-15, start of Italian summer holiday period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 12% indicating population return to urban areas.
